question.prompt: When \(\left(1-\dfrac1a\right)^6\) is expanded, the sum of the last three coefficients is:

solutions.explanation:
For \(a\ne0\), expand in increasing powers of \(1/a\). The last three terms come from choosing \(-1/a\) from four, five, or six of the six factors. By the binomial theorem, they are
\[
\binom64\left(-\frac1a\right)^4
+\binom65\left(-\frac1a\right)^5
+\binom66\left(-\frac1a\right)^6
=\frac{15}{a^4}-\frac6{a^5}+\frac1{a^6}.
\]
Here \(\binom64=\binom62=6\cdot5/2=15\), while the other two binomial coefficients are \(6\) and \(1\). Including the signs, the requested sum is \(15-6+1=\boxed{10}\), choice C.
solutions.title: Extract the last three terms
